source_text: Ὅταν δὲ τὰς λέξεις τῶν προφητῶν λεγομένας ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου ἀκούητε, μὴ (??)π᾿ αὐτῶν τῶν ἐμπεπνευσμένων λέγεσθαι νομίσητε, ἀλλ᾿ ἀπὸ τοῦ κινοῦντος αὐτοὺς θείου λόγου. Ποτὲ μὲν γὰρ ὡς προαγγελτικῶς τὰ μέλλοντα γενήσεσθαι λέγει, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ δεσπότου πάντων καὶ πατρὸς θεοῦ φθέγγεται, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ Χριστοῦ, ποτὲ δὲ ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου λαῶν ἀποκρινομένων τῷ κυρίῳ ἢ τῷ πατρὶ αὐτοῦ· ὁποῖον καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν συγγραφέων ἰδεῖν ἔστιν, ἕνα μὲν τὸν τὰ πάντα συγγράφοντα ὄντα, πρόσωπα δὲ τὰ διαλεγόμενα παραφέροντα. Ὅπερ μὴ νοήσαντες οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς βίβλους τῶν προφητῶν Ἰουδαῖοι οὐκ ἐγνώρισαν οὐδὲ παραγενόμενον τὸν Χριστόν, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡμᾶς τοὺς λέγοντας παραγεγενῆσθαι αὐτὸν καί, ὡς προεκεκήρυκτο, ἀποδεικνύντας ἐσταυρῶσθαι ὑπ᾿ αὐτῶν μισοῦσιν.
pass_a_gloss: When you hear the words of the prophets being spoken as if from a person, do not think they are being said by them, even the inspired ones, but rather from the divine Word moving them. For sometimes He speaks prophetically the things that are going to happen, sometimes as if from the person of the Lord of all and Father God He utters, sometimes as if from the person of Christ, sometimes as if from the person of peoples responding to the Lord or to His Father; a thing of this kind can also be seen in the writings among you, one being the writer of all, but the persons conversing being introduced. Which thing the Jews, having the books of the prophets, not having understood, did not recognize the Christ when He came, but they also hate us who say He has come and, as was previously proclaimed, demonstrate that He was crucified by them.
pass_b_english: When you hear the prophets' words spoken as if from a person, do not suppose that even the inspired prophets themselves are the ones speaking; rather, it is the divine Word that moves them. For at one time He speaks prophetically of things to come; at another, He utters words as if from the person of the Lord of all and Father God; at another, as if from the person of Christ; at another, as if from the person of peoples answering the Lord or His Father. You can see the same thing in your own writers: a single author writes the whole, yet introduces many speaking persons. Because the Jews who possessed the prophetic books failed to grasp this, they did not recognize the Christ when He came, and they hate us who declare that He has come and, as was foretold, prove that He was crucified by them.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, particularly the distinction between the divine mover and the inspired persons. The handling of 'ἀπὸ προσώπου' as 'as if from the person' is appropriate for the context of literary/prophetic persona. The translation of 'ὅποῖον καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν συγγραφέων ἰδεῖν ἔστιν' is rendered faithfully in both passes. The OCR uncertainty '(??)π᾿' in the Greek is ignored as per instructions.
